correctness.rationale: Area(K+H)=Area(K)+Area(H)+sum_{edges e of K}|e|h_H(normal_e) for full planar convex polygons. Regular edge normals sample the support of the reflected rotated regular m-gon. The gcd reduction yields g repetitions of an n/g-term cosine sequence with step 2pi/lcm(n,m). Explicit odd/even finite cosine progression summation establishes the claimed angular profile at all boundary/tie cases. Monotonicity of cosine gives all global equality directions and distribution by uniform nearest-lattice distance. Independent convex-hull calculations passed 559 arbitrary-angle and predicted-extremum cases, but the proof establishes all integer orders.

originality.rationale: The proof derives a complete all-pairs relative-angle cosine lattice profile, gcd/lcm extremum law and full pushforward distribution. The 2026 binary regular-polygon adsorption manuscript reports fixed-orientation analyses and same-species formulas, not the arbitrary-angle all-mixed-order theorem. A classical mixed-area identity is acknowledged as prior, and it alone does not state the arithmetic evaluation. value.rationale: The excluded area is the natural geometric input in planar binary hard-polygon mixture models. The result determines the complete orientation response for every two species, and all sharp extrema and the random-orientation law, with a nontrivial gcd/lcm selection rule and cusp minima. It genuinely extends finite mixture computations rather than recomputing a few entries. The exact invariant and its distinction between smooth maxima and cusp minima are independently motivated.
